In multi-task reinforcement learning, agents often encounter the challenge of task interference, where knowledge gained from one task negatively impacts performance on another. This issue is particularly pronounced in model-based multi-task reinforcement learning, where the agent's ability to learn from one task can lead to catastrophic interference in its underlying models, hindering performance on other tasks. To address this challenge, we propose a novel modular network architecture that isolates task-specific information within each module, thereby preventing interference across tasks. Our approach is grounded in theoretical analysis and supported by empirical evidence, demonstrating that modular networks can effectively mitigate task interference and improve performance on multiple tasks. Our results show that modular networks outperform traditional approaches in both single-task and multi-task reinforcement learning scenarios, and our code is available for public use. Our findings also highlight the importance of model-based methods in multi-task reinforcement learning, particularly when tasks exhibit varying levels of similarity.
